sections.h2: What does the Hamblen County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds keeps the public record of who owns what in Hamblen County. When a house sells, the deed goes to this office, gets stamped with a book and page number, and becomes part of the chain of title that any later buyer or lender will search. The office also takes in trust deeds, releases of old mortgages, powers of attorney, charters, plats and military discharges.

The county says its records reach back to 1860. Staff are still scanning deeds and plats into electronic form, working back to 1978, so older instruments may need a trip to the counter or a call before they turn up online.

The Register also collects two taxes on behalf of the Tennessee Department of Revenue: the realty transfer tax on land sales and the mortgage tax on debt instruments. Those two taxes make up most of the money that changes hands at the counter.

sections.h2: Where is the Hamblen County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?
sections.html:
The office is on the third floor of the Administrative Building at the Hamblen County Courthouse, 511 West Second North Street, Morristown, TN 37814. The phone is 423-586-6551 and the fax is 423-318-2505.

Hamblen County is small in area, 176 square miles with 161 of them land, and the courthouse stands in Morristown, the county seat. The Census Bureau counts 68,843 residents as of July 2025, 28,945 housing units and 258 building permits issued during 2025. Median owner-occupied home value is $210,900 for 2020 to 2024.

Before you go, have these items ready:

  • The signed deed, ready for the buyer or the buyer's representative to swear to the price or value in front of the Register
  • The parcel details from the Assessor, who is in the same courthouse at 423-586-1852
  • For a modified or amended deed, the book and page of the earlier recorded document
  • Payment for the recording fee and the tax

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Hamblen County?
sections.html:
Recording fees are set by state statute and are the same in every county, so the figures below come from the county technical assistance service's summary of the register's standard fees. Military discharges are recorded free of charge.

ItemFeeSource
Standard document, up to two pages$10.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees
Each page after the second$5.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees
Each extra instrument in one document$5.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees
Plat, map or survey$15.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees
Data processing fee per instrument$2.00UT CTAS, Data Processing Fee
Receipt for state tax$1.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees
Certified copy of a document, per page$1.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees

A four-page deed therefore costs $20 in page fees, $2 for data processing and $1 for the tax receipt, or $23, before the tax itself. Page size may not exceed 8 1/2 by 14 inches.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Hamblen County home sale?
sections.html:
The realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the price, which is 0.37 percent. The Department of Revenue bases it on the greater of what was paid or what the property is worth when it changes hands. The buyer, called the grantee on the deed, is the person the statute makes responsible for paying it, and the register collects it where the instrument is offered for recording.

A worked example uses the county's median home value. At $210,900 the tax is 2,109 hundreds times $0.37, or $780.33. Add the $23 in recording charges from the four-page deed above and the courthouse total is $803.33. Closing statements often show who covers it, so check yours with the title company.

The deed must carry a sworn statement of the actual price or value, made by the buyer or the buyer's representative in front of the Register. A knowingly false statement is treated as perjury. The state also reviews recorded deeds from time to time and compares the sworn value with the assessor's figure, which can lead to a letter from the Department of Revenue. The department accepts the assessor's tax base, or a recent appraisal the assessor's office has accepted, as fair market value.

sections.h2: Which Hamblen County transfers are exempt from transfer tax?
sections.html:
State law lists transfers that pay no realty transfer tax. The Department of Revenue's manual names these among them:

  • A conveyance from one spouse to the other, or one that creates or ends a tenancy by the entirety
  • A deed from an executor carrying out a will
  • Transfers under a divorce decree or domestic settlement
  • A transfer into a revocable living trust by its creator or the creator's spouse, and back out again
  • Distributions by a trustee to the beneficiaries under a will or a revocable trust
  • Transfers to or from a government body

No oath is required on an exempt transfer. Quitclaim deeds are treated carefully: the tax base is the consideration given, unless the wording shows an intent to convey the property itself, such as language saying to have and to hold or in fee simple, in which case the market value applies.

sections.h2: What is the mortgage tax and who pays it in Hamblen County?
sections.html:
The mortgage tax, which the Department of Revenue also calls the indebtedness tax, applies when a deed of trust is recorded. The rate is $0.115 per $100 of debt, and the first $2,000 is exempt. The borrower pays it to the Register along with the recording fee.

For a buyer financing $168,000, the taxable amount is $166,000 and the tax comes to $190.90. The instrument has to state, on its face or in an attached sworn statement, the sentence reading Maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee Recording tax purposes is a dollar amount. The register cannot record the instrument until that statement is present and the tax is paid.

Loan assumptions are treated in two ways. If a buyer promises to pay the seller's debt but the seller stays liable, no new tax is due, because no new debt exists. If the buyer signs a new contract with the lender that cancels the seller's obligation, tax is due on the new mortgage.

sections.h2: How can I research a Hamblen County deed or property record?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor of Property, Keith Ely, in the same courthouse. The office keeps ownership, address, deed reference and appraised value for roughly 32,000 parcels and maintains over 400 maps showing property lines and acreage. Then go to the Register for the recorded instruments themselves, using the book and page number from the assessor record.

A certified copy of a document costs $1 a page. Because scanning only reaches back to 1978, ask the office how to search for anything older.

Sellers who plan a quick sale can ask the title company to pull the chain of title early. A deed that was never recorded, a release missing from an old loan, or a name that differs between the deed and the tax roll can hold up a closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Hamblen County Register of Deeds located?
faqs.a: In the Administrative Building at the Hamblen County Courthouse, third floor, 511 West Second North Street, Morristown, TN 37814. The phone is 423-586-6551.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Hamblen County?
faqs.a: A two-page deed is $10, each additional page is $5, and a $2 data processing fee and $1 tax receipt are added. State transfer tax of $0.37 per $100 of value is collected on top.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when a Hamblen County house sells?
faqs.a: The statute makes the buyer, as grantee, responsible and has the Register collect it at recording. The closing statement shows how it was handled. The rate is $0.37 per $100.

faqs.q: Are there deeds that do not need transfer tax in Hamblen County?
faqs.a: Yes. Transfers between spouses, an executor's deed carrying out a will, divorce decree transfers and moves into a revocable living trust are among those listed by the state as not subject to the tax.

faqs.q: Does the Register of Deeds also keep property tax records?
faqs.a: No. Value and tax rolls are with the Assessor of Property at 423-586-1852, and bills are paid to the Trustee at 423-586-6290. The Register records the deed and collects the state recordation taxes.
